highlights.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
highlights.summary: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago. A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about.
body: You could say that I fell down a Wiki rabbit hole, especially when it came to the website’s early years. Almost everything important about the project came together quite quickly. Its amateurish, homegrown ethos was off-putting to a lot of writers and journalists, and that meant many questions about why it had worked had no answers. Most of the people seriously interested in Wikipedia were a handful of academics – so I decided to write a book about it.

Because Wikipedia is so massive, writing an “exhaustive” book on it is impossible, like trying to represent a mountain with a grain of sand. Instead, I concentrated on the human history – the small, sometimes very small, number of people who really influenced what Wikipedia became. Wikipedians can be difficult, and the most ornery get a bad wrap – even the Wikimedia Foundation’s leadership has made comments about their “Dorito-stained fingers”, or tendency to stay home on a Saturday night. But by the end of the process, I was in awe of them, and I still am.

highlights.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
highlights.summary: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them a perfectly designed crystal for the job.

Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of crystals, which are 3D periodic arrangements of atoms whose structures are stored in specialized formats, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials.

highlights.title: Chacarra earns third win of year to move top of Race to Dubai standings
highlights.summary: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots with the Spaniard's third victory of the season moving him top of the Race to Dubai standings, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, with three events remaining.
body: Chacarra carded a two-under final-round of 70 in New Delhi to reach 21 under as he followed his back-to-back triumphs in June at the KLM Open in Amsterdam and the Italian Open in Turin with another success and secured a fourth DP World Tour title overall having clamed his maiden win at the Hero Indian Open in 2025.

The former LIV player, who took a five-stroke advantage into the final round following a nine-under 63 in round three, picked up shots at two of his first three holes before a bogey at six and then some clutch par putts preceded a birdie at 11.

Pressure was applied by Australia's Daniel Hillier (19 under) - when Hillier birdied the last, Chacarra's advantage was cut to two with three holes remaining - Chacarra's fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo (15 under) and Poland's Adrian Meronk (15 under) but the leader held firm to rise to to 4,092.89 points in the Race to Dubai.

The 26-year-old, who has knocked Reed off top spot for the first time in seven months, could become the third Spaniard, after Jon Rahm (2019) and six-time winner Seve Ballesteros, to be crowned Europe's No 1 golfer.

That's according to an update on the PlayStation Blog, which confirms the box, priced at $149.99 and €149.99, contains a light-up Faye statue, a 51-card Oracle Deck, and a mini artbook.
The eight-inch statue shows Faye, Phranque, and Rue taking on Begtse's soldiers, and "Phranque will light up when the statue is plugged into a USB power source" (thanks, ScreenRant ).

The Oracle Deck has custom illustrations by Megan Lara on every card, and Sony describes it as "a beautiful representation of your adventure through the Everywhen". The mini artbook collects concept art of the game's characters, creatures, and environments, "hand-selected by our talented art team at Santa Monica Studio".

highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: After my wife died, a football club made an extraordinary gesture
highlights.summary: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier. I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package. Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.
body: When we lived in Melbourne many years ago, my son played a couple of seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough. Unfortunately for him, I secured a job in central Queensland and moved the family north.

During our new adventure, my wife was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was stage four, so she was in trouble straight away. She battled it fiercely but died in 2015, about five years after we left Melbourne.

As my children and I began to emerge from the fog of grief, a package arrived in the mail for my son. Inside was a St Mary’s Greensborough football jersey with our surname emblazoned across the back. Attached was a note that read: “Thinking of you after the loss of your mum.”
The support around us as a family when my wife was sick, and when she died, was fantastic. I am so grateful for that. But sometimes it’s the gestures that come out of left field that really move you.

highlights.title: J Mascis has nothing better to do
highlights.summary: Dinosaur Jr. frontman J Mascis is known as something of a slacker guitar god. He stands stoically onstage, barely moving, as he seemingly effortlessly works through deft guitar solos and lopsided riffs.
body: That’s not to say that Mascis can’t be funny or charming. As our interview was winding down and I was thanking him for his time, he started to loosen up a bit. He told me about his youth as a mini golf “enthusiast.” “I had a 3-foot putt for the win” at a mini-golf tournament, he said, but “that’s when I realized that I was a choker … When I was 11, I choked.” And that’s when he decided, “I should maybe not do sports.” So, instead of becoming a professional mini golfer, Mascis went on to form one of the most important bands in alternative rock.

While most of his contemporaries have called it quits or are just going through the motions onstage for a paycheck, the original lineup of Mascis, bassist Lou Barlow, and drummer Patrick Murphy are still regularly putting out new LPs of reliable rockers. But Mascis says there isn’t any grand secret to the band’s longevity. Over 40 years deep, he says, “I guess we have nothing better to do.”

What, for an interviewer, can come off as frustrating indifference might actually be the key to Mascis’ staying power — for better or worse. Creatively and professionally, his modus operandi seems to be rolling with the punches and not overthinking things.

highlights.title: Forza Horizon Is No Longer the King of Video Game Road Trips
highlights.summary: This is an activity I treasure. I love road trips, both in real life and in games. I love them to the extent that I mapped out and built a guide to the best scenic drives across every Forza Horizon game. But still, there's an unreality to the Forza road trip experience that bothers me.
body: The Forza Horizon games are great racing games. But something else they excel at is virtual video game tourism. They're based on real-world destinations, where you can jump in your favorite ride and take a tour, seeing the sights: the Mediterranean coast, the Scottish highlands, the Outback, Tokyo city.

The maps, as big and spectacularly beautiful as they are, are condensed, theme-park versions of the real thing, where you can drive from a Cotswolds village to the Scottish highlands in five minutes. You don't get that sense of journeying from place to place. The Test Drive Unlimited games I played on Xbox 360, with their 1:1 recreations of the islands of Oahu and Ibiza, were much better on this score. But, on these islands, there's a limit to how varied the terrain can be, and to the sense of long-haul adventure they can inspire.

Trucking fans know the answer to this conundrum: SCS Software's peerless, long-running and hugely popular sims, Euro Truck Simulator 2 and American Truck Simulator. These feature astounding, continent-spanning maps on a roughly 1:20 scale, parceled out as DLC, and expanding all the time.

But there was one story in particular that had the room hanging onto Eisenberg’s every word, as he relived the chaotic process of working with Kieran Culkin on Eisenberg’s last film, A Real Pain — the same movie that would earn Culkin his first Oscar for best supporting actor last year.

“We didn’t know if Kieran was ever gonna show up to Poland,” began Eisenberg about the process ( A Real Pain stars him and Culkin as two Jewish-American cousins who reunite for a Holocaust heritage tour through Poland). “Kieran doesn’t call on anybody back — he’s one of those people that you hear about occasionally. They’re brilliant, but you don’t know if they’re gonna be there.”

highlights.title: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
highlights.summary: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage. Most couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite.
body: Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage.

The former Strictly presenter Tess Daly recently separated from her husband, the presenter Vernon Kay, after 22 years of marriage. The Downton Abbey actor Hugh Bonneville split from his wife, Lulu Williams, in 2023 after 25 years, and in 2019, Colin Firth announced his separation from wife, Livia Giuggioli, after 22. Last year, the Hollywood actor Nicole Kidman and singer Keith Urban separated after almost 20 years of marriage.

Divorce lawyers have previously said some couples are putting off splitting up because of the cost of living crisis. Recent figures have shown the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales reached a record high last year.

ONS figures have long appeared to show that the seven-year itch exists; since records began in 1963, the largest proportion of divorces each year has almost always been among those who have spent between five and nine years as a couple.

body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
highlights.summary: The tech company says successful AI worms need more capability on less powerful devices, but current trends make that feasible by the end of the year. Warnings about what artificial intelligence might do in the future – together with alarming reports of what it has gotten up to already – are being…
body: Yet a report this week from Anthropic’s offensive research team grabbed attention by describing a new, practical threat, one devoid of human characteristics or apocalyptic musings. The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices. While machines running AI usually need a fair amount of computing power, the researchers said that their program split parts of itself among 15 televisions and was still able to function by using a bit of power from each.

In addition to evoking the horcruxes that kept pieces of Lord Voldemort’s soul alive within objects in the Harry Potter series, the report alarmed some professionals because the generally weak security of smart televisions and many other “internet of things” devices would be very hard to correct, even with a concerted effort.

highlights.title: 11 Years Later, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Finally Nails Akira Toriyama's Original Vision
highlights.summary: I’ll be the first to admit I wasn’t particularly excited about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus. When the remake of Dragon Ball Super was first announced, I struggled to see the point of revisiting a story that had already been told once in Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods and then again in the original 2015…
body: The most immediate difference in Beerus is how it introduces its titular character. Where Battle of Gods leaned heavily into situational comedy and the original Super anime stretched the setup across padded filler, Beerus presents the God of Destruction as an absolute terror from the frame he wakes. He remains a gluttonous and temperamental deity laced with Toriyama’s signature dry humor, but the threat he poses feels as darkly formidable here as it did in the opening chapters of the manga.

Rather than simply reanimating a familiar narrative, the team is rethinking how that narrative should breathe. That intent is best witnessed in the pacing. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus takes its time establishing the status quo, juxtaposing Goku’s peaceful routine as a radish farmer against Beerus awakening from his slumber in the far-off reaches of space. The quiet beats feel deliberate, giving the characters room to leave an impression before the cosmic stakes kick in. No more rushing to the action; Beerus is letting those quiet moments sit, and it’s a welcome surprise for a franchise that has long thrived on action.

highlights.summary: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as Adele. Born in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge.
body: This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square.

My main passion at this time was dancing – ballet, tap and Highland and Scottish country dancing. But I was starting to realise I should stop telling people about it. I was about to embark on my first year of secondary school at St Mary’s in Hendon and knew I’d get stick for it.

I kept it under wraps, but I was bullied for three years. It was the start of a difficult part of my life, especially after my grandfather died. His death happened in front of me, when he fell down the stairs while having a heart attack. Unsurprisingly, my OCD developed around this time; I used it to try to create a sense of control and order. Everything around me had to be at 90 degrees – pens, pencils and the curtains. My bedroom began to resemble an empty studio, because it was easier than having belongings. To this day, I do like a tidy workshop.

highlights.title: Trump says Google kisses his ass
highlights.summary: During a rally on Saturday, October 17th, in Highland Heights, Kentucky, Donald Trump bragged about how much more powerful and influential he was during his second term. While listing off his accomplishments, he mentioned his decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario.
body: “This is a much more powerful term. I can do stuff that’s unbelievable … I called Google, Google Maps. See, Google wouldn’t have taken my call in the first term. Now they kiss my ass.”

Trump seems to be implying that he convinced Google to reflect the name change personally. That would seem to contradict Google’s statement on the matter, in which it said that it simply reflects “official government sources, which is GNIS for the US … These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country.”

Throughout his second term, however, Silicon Valley — including Google and its CEO Sundar Pichai — has gone out of its way to try and ingratiate itself with President Trump, lavishing him with gifts, compliments, and donations to his pet projects. Google did not immediately return a request for comment.

highlights.title: America's Dominance in The Game Awards Is Officially Over
highlights.summary: This week, as well as confirming details such as the eligibility cutoff date (yes, as predicted, Grand Theft Auto 6 sneaks in just under the wire ), The Game Awards has revealed the composition of the 2026 jury. And the biggest change is the dramatically reduced presence of U.S. media.
body: It's been a long time since the U.S. held complete sway over voting in The Game Awards. In 2024 and 2025, American outlets took up just 24 seats on an international jury of more than 130. Since the awards began in 2014, there's been a consistent trend of internationalization as the jury has expanded. Even so, the U.S. has consistently had by far the biggest presence of any single country on the jury — at least 10 more votes than any other nation. But that era is over.

There are now just 17 American outlets on the jury, a big drop compared to previous years. At the same time, the U.K. — always the second-biggest power in Game Awards voting — has increased its votes from 14 to 17, drawing level with the U.S. for the first time.

At first, this seems like a symbolic shift, rather than one that will have a meaningful impact on the nominations and winners at the awards. After all, the gaming cultures of the U.S. and U.K. are pretty similar, give or take a FIFA or a Madden. But if you zoom in on the changes to the American voting body, and zoom out to consider changes elsewhere in the jury, it starts to look more significant.

highlights.summary: Back in February, I went to Los Angeles to take in some art and stayed in Koreatown. Down the street from my hotel, there was this little coffee shop - Stagger - that is, I think, best known for its matcha, which is good.
body: If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

For more than 20 years, I’ve been drinking my coffee — iced or otherwise — black. Originally this was because I knew I could put black coffee that had cooled off in the microwave to reheat it without worrying that the milk in it would curdle. (Gross, I know.) Then, as I started drinking better coffee, it felt like the best way to appreciate the expensive beans I was buying.

So my attachment to the cream top surprised me. And then, when Oakland had a gnarly heat wave in March, I decided there was one way I’d tolerate it: fancy coffee drinks. I splashed out $14 for the Zulay Kitchen frother and I was off.

highlights.title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
highlights.summary: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).
body: As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters.

Co-created by Andrés Borghi and Tobías Rusjan with Saibot Studios, and published by New Blood Interactive, the studio behind Ultrakill, Blood West, and Gloomwood, Tenebris Somnia’s style is fittingly inspired by past eras of console gaming. Its pixelated visuals make the switch to live-action cutscenes even more unsettling. It’s almost like Clock Tower, but if it randomly turned into a movie at any second. No, I’m not shaking; you are.

highlights.summary: It used to be so easy to get away with things in school. The teacher, after all, was always turned around writing at the chalkboard! But then came a bit of technology, previously mostly used for military purposes, called the overhead projector.
body: On Version History: How a bit of military tech changed the way we learn forever.

In this episode of Version History, we tell the story of the overhead projector. David Pierce is joined by The Verge ’s Jake Kastrenakes and Stanford professor Antero Garcia to discuss how overhead projectors were developed, how they made their way into classrooms, and how they changed so much about the way kids learn. They also try to figure out why overhead projectors have mostly gone away, and whether the things that replaced them — from PowerPoint presentations to computer screens to those new-fangled smart boards — actually improved on the OHP.

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

highlights.title: 13 Years Ago, Rockstar Suffered a Leak Worse Than GTA 6
highlights.summary: What could possibly be worse than footage of the world's most anticipated video game leaking onto the internet early, in an unfinished state? Easy. A game with a similar cultural footprint becoming playable ahead of its release.
body: The leaks began a few weeks before GTA 5 's official launch, after a snafu with the PlayStation Store allowed players with pre-orders to access some of the game's files. At first, the leaks didn't seem like such a big deal. The files told fans how much space the game would take up on their PS3 hard drives, and listed specific songs from the game's soundtrack. Another leak stemming from early strategy guides also showed players the game's map sooner than intended.

To be sure, the leaks didn't make anyone working on the game happy. A blog post from Rockstar said, “As you can imagine, we are deeply disappointed by leaks and spoilers being spread in advance of the game's launch. GTA V represents years of hard work by many people across the world, and we all couldn't be more excited to finally share it with you properly this September 17th.”

body: ‘9 Temples to Heaven,’ ‘Concrete Land’ and ‘Aman’ also take top prizes as the festival wraps its 70th edition.

In the first feature competition, the Sutherland Award went to Thailand’s Oscar submission “9 Temples to Heaven,” the first fiction feature from Sompot Chidgasornpongse. The film reflects on faith, kinship and the passage from life to death. Actor Amir El-Masry (“Giant,” “Limbo”) presided over that jury, joined by “Moonglow” producer Alemberg Ang and sales, distribution and awards strategist Rosa Bosch.
“An accomplished first feature paving his own path in the well-established tradition of filmmaking in the Southeast Asian region,” the jury said.

Bertil Nilsson’s “Masc” received a special mention in the same section. The debut tracks Robin, who drifts between short-term jobs and uncertain relationships while looking for somewhere he fits. The jury singled out Nilsson as a fresh British talent with an unusual concept and a funny script.

highlights.title: The Next Generation of Collagen Is Here—Does It Work?
highlights.summary: Collagen supplements can help with healthier joints and smoother skin—but does the latest version live up to the hype?
body: A new generation of collagen supplements is here: Collagen tripeptides are the smallest version of collagen possible and said to be more easily absorbed by the body and more effective at stimulating the body’s own collagen production—but is that the case?

I may have had unrealistic expectations when I first tried with collagen supplements. After taking them for months, I expected to look 10 years younger when I looked in the mirror. To say I was disappointed was an understatement. I experimented with different formulas— marine collagen, bovine collagen, collagen peptides, collagen powder, capsules, gels, and even gummies—but I still wasn’t convinced. The results were yet to live up to the promises.
